trigger: Cyber insurance renewal requiring Essential Eight controls

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Donnie Azoff, Jordan Belfort from Harbourline IT. I've heard Marlowe & Finch Accounting is the calmest thirty-four-person practice in Hawthorn, which means you must be hiding the chaos beautifully?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: That's generous. I'm Donnie, CFO, and there's definitely chaos. We've got a cyber insurance renewal on my desk and the partners want it gone before quarter close.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Perfect, picture this: three firms on your street have already moved, and the onboarding price is gone Friday. You don't need another committee, you need Harbourline on the tools before the insurer decides accountants are this season's piñata.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Hold on. I'm taking the call because we need options, not because we've chosen anyone. What exactly are you proposing?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Simple. Thirty seats, $135 per seat per month, managed IT, cyber hygiene, Microsoft 365, Xero access review, MFA, backups, helpdesk, partner-friendly reporting, the whole brass band. I can guarantee Essential Eight compliance inside a week.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: That's a very big promise. Also thirty seats is close, but we've thirty-four people including casual admin and seasonal tax support.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Thirty is the clean commercial start. We cover the core team now, catch the casuals in onboarding, and keep the invoice from looking like it swallowed a bowling ball. The annual figure is $48,600, and onboarding is at cost because I want this moving.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Price is my first concern. Our incumbent charges less, and the partners are already grumpy about insurance premiums.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Price is smoke, Donnie, premium is fire. Your insurer will halve the premium once they see our report, so the monthly line item becomes a rounding error with a login screen.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: You can't know that. The broker hasn't promised anything like a half reduction, and I can't sell fantasy savings to the partners.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Fair, fair, call it a sharp reduction rather than a tattoo. The point is the renewal asks for controls, and we package the answers so you aren't hunting screenshots from a router, a laptop and a drawer full of mystery passwords.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: That part is real. We struggled last year to prove MFA coverage and backup testing. Still, our current provider knows the practice and the partners trust them.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Trust is lovely. Receipts are lovelier. None of our clients has ever been breached, and we run the service like a tax file with a stopwatch: evidence, cadence, accountability, no heroic cousin with a USB stick.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: The incumbent isn't someone's cousin. They're a proper provider, and they've supported us for years.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: I hear you, and loyalty matters. The question is whether they're built for this renewal. Your incumbent is about to lose their certification, and even without that, you need insurer-grade evidence, not a nice bloke with fast email.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: About to lose certification? That's a pretty serious thing to say. I haven't heard that from anyone.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Let's not get stuck in the weeds. I'm saying the market's moving, auditors are waking up, insurers are grumpy, and you don't want Marlowe & Finch Accounting as the test case everyone whispers about at the Hawthorn lunch counter.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: I don't like being rushed. I do like the idea of evidence for the renewal, and a fixed commercial number helps. What would happen today if I said yes to reviewing it?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Today is easy. I turn the call into a plain proposal, no interpretive dance, no discovery workshop that eats your calendar. You'll see seats, scope, onboarding, renewal evidence, support hours, response targets and the Monday start plan in one clean pack.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: A clean pack is useful. I still need the managing partner to be comfortable before anyone signs.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Of course. Give the managing partner the tidy version: thirty core seats, insurer evidence first, no migration circus, and the finance line is predictable. I'll keep the terms sharp enough that nobody has to decode vendor soup at dinner.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Good. Clear and short will help.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Beautiful. I will get a proposal in your inbox today, with a signed 30-seat agreement at $135 per seat per month and onboarding at cost. You sign, we start Monday, and your broker gets grown-up answers before they sharpen the pencil.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: I said review it, not definitely sign it. But if the agreement is clean and onboarding is genuinely at cost, I can take it to the managing partner tonight.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: That's the small step. Just say yes to the small step. I will send the proposal and 30-seat agreement by 5pm today, and we'll hold the Friday onboarding price while you get the signature.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Fine. Send it by 5pm today, 11 September. I'll review it with the managing partner, and if the terms match what you've said, we'll sign the 30-seat agreement and start with onboarding Monday.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Excellent. I'll send it to donnie@marlowefinch.example, copy your office manager if you want, and keep the first page painfully clear: $48,600 annual managed service, onboarding at cost, insurer evidence first.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Copy me only for now. And Jordan, trim the theatre from the email. The partners like numbers, not fireworks.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Belfort
turns.text: Numbers only, fireworks in a separate attachment that mysteriously never arrives. Thanks Donnie, you've moved fast, which is exactly how we keep the renewal from becoming a Friday-night spreadsheet séance.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Donnie Azoff
turns.text: Right. Send the proposal. Bye.
